ASSIGNMENT AND RESERVATION I have been asked to provide expert opinions, on behalf of Plaintiff, Kathleen Moller, regarding the wrongful death of her daughter, Harmony Moller. This report opines on Ms. Moller’s death and the cause of her death, including the impact of and causative nature of Defendants’ OPMS brand kratom products. I reserve the right to rephrase or alter my opinions as additional information is received. I reserve the right to supplement this report when further data, documents, or information becomes available and/or to correct it if errors are discovered. Further, at trial, I may use visual aids or demonstrative exhibits, such as diagrams, images, slides, or charts that illustrate and/or explain my opinions. II. QUALIFICATIONS I am a licensed medical doctor practicing in the state of Florida with Board Certifications in Emergency Medicine, Medical Toxicology, and Occupational and Environmental Medicine. I have over 20 years of clinical experience with

OPINIONS AND BASIS THEREOF These opinions are given to a reasonable degree of medical certainty. a. Harmony Moller’s cause of death was an adverse cardiorespiratory event caused by kratom. Kratom is the common term for Mitragyna speciosa, a tree that is native to Southeast Asia. In traditional preparations, kratom leaves are used in tea as an herbal medicine for various medical conditions including pain and increased energy. In the United States, the commercially sold kratom often takes the form of processed powders and extracts. Both the effect and toxicity of kratom are dose related.

Case 2:24-cv-00228-WBV-DPC Document 267-62 Filed 03/02/26 Page 10 of 49 Kratom is considered a drug of concern by the US Drug Enforcement Administration, and the FDA has issued an Import Alert identifying kratom as a New Dietary Ingredient (NDI) for which a reasonable expectation of safety has not been established. Kratom leaves produce over 25 alkaloid compounds. The most prominent psychoactive components are: (1) mitragynine (MTG); and (2) 7- hydroxymitragynine (7HMG). Both MTG and 7HMG are agonists at the mu-opioid receptor. 7HMG is considered nine times more active than MTG. Clinical effects of mitragynine are in part related to the mu-opioid receptor activity, additionally mitragynine has been reported to bind to other receptors including adrenergic, serotonin and dopamine receptors. Kratom has polypharmacologic activity including stimulant, opioid, and sedative type effects. Both the effect and toxicity of kratom are dose related. Documented symptoms include but are not limited to respiratory depression, cardiac arrythmias, prolonged QT, seizures, liver impairment, and psychosis. Regular consumption of kratom is associated with tolerance and dependency, requiring ingestion of higher doses to achieve similar effect. Kratom related deaths involve clinical findings consistent with opioid toxicity, intractable seizures, and cardiorespiratory arrest. Often, when an individual dies from elevated opiate levels, the cause is properly attributed to a chronic dependency leading to escalated doses that exceed therapeutic levels. The same process occurs with kratom, with the important exception that those selling the kratom frequently do not provide warnings or safe instructions for use and dosing. This includes drug interactions or interactions with underlying health conditions. Kratom’s adverse effects include severe dependence negatively affecting physical well-being and opioid-like withdrawal symptoms requiring medical intervention after addiction to kratom. A case report of an individual using kratom for chronic pain documented a pattern of daily kratom consumption in which tolerance development for analgesic effects was overcome by an increase in daily consumption. Ultimately, the high kratom dosing provided less relief and started to induce fatigue and drowsiness and rather prevented the patient from work and an active lifestyle. The patient ultimately required professional help for kratom withdrawal. Kratom also acts as a stimulant. Stimulants like kratom have the potential to cause enlargement of the heart. An enlarged heart is a heart that is electrically susceptible to arrythmias. The stimulant effects of kratom increase the likelihood of electrical instability and sudden cardiac death. The stimulant effect of kratom has

On February 6, 2023, Harmony Moller (DOB: 02/18/1986) was discovered by her mother, Kathleen Moller, unresponsive in her bedroom. Nearby, Defendants’ kratom products were discovered. Paramedics were called. EMS records note Harmony was in asystole, and resuscitation was attempted via compressions and ventilation. However, Ms. Moller remained without any pulse, any cardiac activity, or spontaneous respirations or movements, and she was therefore pronounced dead. The investigation by law enforcement and the medical examiner did not find signs of foul play or suicide. The foregoing context supports the conclusion that Harmony Moller died from an adverse cardiorespiratory event caused by kratom. My review of the medical and death records stated above included findings of pulmonary edema and congestion, chronic passive congestion of the liver, and mild nephrosclerosis, high origin of left coronary artery, and cardiomegaly. Cardiomegaly is a finding that Harmony’s heart was enlarged. As noted above, enlargement of the heart may be caused by repetitive use of stimulants, like kratom. These conditions may have been co-morbidities for Harmony Moller but were not the primary cause of death. The primary cause of death was a cardiorespiratory event caused by kratom. The toxicology results from NMS Labs directly support kratom’s causative role in Harmony’s death. The blood concentration of Mitragynine was 150 ng/ml, a level sufficient to cause adverse events. A blood concentration of 7- hydroxymitragynine at 0.8 ng/ml was also present. The toxicology results also returned a positive result for caffeine, a finding expected in individual who ingested caffeinated products such as coffee. Naloxone was also positive. The naloxone was administered by first aid responders according to EMS records. Delta-9 THC and Delta-9 Carboxy THC were also present at low levels. These concentrations are not consistent with a toxic or fatal ingestion. Diphenhydramine was present at a concentration of 64 ng/ml. Said concentration is not consistent with a fatal or toxic dose. Promethazine was present at a concentration of 18 ng/ml. Said concentration is not consistent with a fatal or toxic dose. The concentrations of diphenhydramine and promethazine are consistent with therapeutic dosing, and therefore unlikely to be a cause or contributor of Harmony Moller’s death. The toxicology results confirm that the cause of death was directly related to kratom. I conclude from the historical context, the medical examiner’s report, the heart pathology report, and the toxicology results that kratom caused the adverse cardiorespiratory death of Harmony Moller. This conclusion is being made with a reasonable degree of medical certainty.
